solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Teacher after clemency for army officer

indicators.note: one thing coming after another sets the order, so the second-named piece is placed later in the answer

blocks.note: to give quarter is to show mercy to a defeated enemy
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher follows a plea for mercy on behalf of a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the teacher first, but 'after' puts that piece second.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the officer responsible for supplies, rations and lodging in a regiment.

clue.text: Not stooping to dishonesty

blocks.note: surface reading: someone too principled to lower themselves to cheating
setter's reading: literally standing straight, not bent over, which is also the word for an honest person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stooping' works both as bending the body and as lowering one's standards; the answer covers the straight posture and the straight character.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honourable and law-abiding, and an upright post stands vertically without bending.

clue.text: A knot that seamen consider dangerous

blocks.note: first meaning: the square knot used by sailors to tie two ropes
second meaning: a ridge of rock or coral just below the sea surface

explanation.surface: A sailor warns that a certain knot is not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests one knot that sailors dislike; in fact the knot and the hazard are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is a standard sailing tie, and a submerged rock ridge wrecks ships, so sailors fear it.

clue.text: Yes, cats may produce this feeling in people

indicators.note: to produce something is to make it out of raw material, so the letters are worked into a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cat lovers agree that their pets bring on a warm feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma and 'Yes' read as agreement, but both words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is an overwhelming emotion of joy or rapture that a person can experience.

clue.text: Island‘s chief accountant

blocks.note: major means main or chief
CA is chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An island's senior accountant is being introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's reads as ownership but it is simply 'is' linking definition to wordplay. CA stands for chartered accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is the largest of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean, belonging to Spain.

clue.text: Initially supplied second-hand, now disposed of

indicators.note: initially means at the very start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the word
second-hand goods are old, previously used

explanation.surface: Goods once bought used have now been got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-hand' is not about a clock or a hand; it simply means old.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that have been sold have been disposed of by passing them to a buyer for money.

clue.text: Allowed to be clever in the finish

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the end is the finish
able means capable, clever

explanation.surface: Someone is finally permitted to show their brilliance at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clever in the finish' reads as a late flourish, but 'in' is the instruction to put one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable someone is to make them able to do something, so being enabled is being permitted.

clue.text: No relations of newly-weds

blocks.note: surface reading: people who are not family members of a just-married couple
setter's reading: relations are stories that are related, and these ones are told not by new brides but by long-married women

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like in-laws but means accounts or narratives; 'No ... newly-weds' points to wives who are not new, which is old.
explanation.definitionFit: Old wives' tales are traditional superstitious beliefs or folk stories passed down, usually untrue.

clue.text: Dare any health resorts residents walk out like this?

indicators.note: read as re-sorts, it means sorts again, putting the letters into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spa resort challenges its guests to leave in rude good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Health resorts' reads as spas, but 'resorts' is a verb meaning sorts again, working on the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hale and hearty describes a person who is strong, vigorous and in robust physical condition.

clue.text: Bounty, big ship

blocks.note: large means big
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: The Bounty, a famous mutiny vessel, is described as a big ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bounty is the ship of the famous mutiny, which makes 'big ship' look like its description; in fact 'Bounty' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving of money or gifts, the same idea as a bounty or handout.

clue.text: Roman emperor linked with a late former queen

blocks.note: Julian the Apostate was a fourth-century Roman emperor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historian connects an ancient emperor with a royal lady of recent times.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface but gives just its own letter before the definition begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliana was Queen of the Netherlands from 1948 until she abdicated in 1980; she died in 2004.

clue.text: Payment we will take in silver

indicators.note: to take something in is to receive it inside, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Workers agree to be paid in silver coins.
explanation.walkthrough: WE wraps around AG, the symbol for silver from Latin argentum.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is the regular money paid to an employee for work done.

clue.text: Grain leaving tropic island

indicators.note: something that is leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: the Tropic of Capricorn is a line of latitude
corn is grain

explanation.surface: A cargo of grain is shipped away from a tropical island.
explanation.walkthrough: Tropic points to Capricorn, the southern tropic; take the grain out of it and what is left is the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, off southern Italy.

clue.text: Run away, having got left in charge

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a fee is a charge
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone bolts after being put in charge and left to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge' looks like responsibility, but charge is a fee, with L put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to escape or run away from danger or a place.

clue.text: Kind of girl to give Rex the quick run around

indicators.note: going around something surrounds it, so one piece is wrapped about the other

blocks.note: a flit is a quick darting movement
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A girl gives a man called Rex the runaround.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex looks like a man's name, but it is Latin for king and gives R, which sits inside the quick run.
explanation.definitionFit: A flirt is someone who playfully teases and leads others on romantically without serious intent.

clue.text: Thrown, we hear, by the class system

indicators.note: what we hear is what is spoken, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: cast means thrown

explanation.surface: Someone feels thrown off course by rigid social hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' could mean confused, but here it is the past participle of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The caste system is the hereditary social hierarchy of Hindu society, dividing people into ranked groups.

clue.text: Score six to open in a forceful way

indicators.note: what opens comes at the start, so that piece is placed at the front

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a tally is a score or count

explanation.surface: A batsman opens the innings by hitting a six in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's 'six' and 'open' make a batting picture, but six is VI, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitally means energetically, with full life and vigour, which approximates acting forcefully.

clue.text: A row about boy appearing in pantomime

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a lad is a boy
a din is a noisy row

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a boy's part in the Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: A and DIN together make A...DIN, which goes about LAD. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families based on fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Aladdin is one of the most popular traditional British Christmas pantomimes, based on the Arabian Nights tale.

clue.text: Pip has taken dog in to be tied up

indicators.note: having taken something in means holding it inside, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a pip is a fruit seed
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone called Pip has taken in a stray dog, and it must be tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pip looks like a name (as in Great Expectations) but is a fruit seed, which takes in the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secured has been fastened firmly, as a boat is tied up to a mooring.

clue.text: Stinging bill rises and is cut unexpectedly

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top, backwards
something that happens unexpectedly departs from the planned order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painful bill goes up, then is unexpectedly cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The bill is an account, AC, which rises to CA; then 'is cut' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Caustic describes a substance that burns chemically, or a remark that is bitingly sarcastic and wounding.

clue.text: The estate needs me for organisation

indicators.note: organisation is the act of arranging things, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A land agent boasts that the estate needs them to run it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' reads as management of the estate, but it asks for the letters to be organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land attached to a manor and kept for the owner's own use, a historic landed property.

clue.text: China to broadcast in town of early Christianity

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are scattered and regathered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: China plans to air programmes in an ancient Christian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio or television, but its older sense of scattering makes it the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch, in modern Turkey, is where followers of Jesus were first called Christians, according to Acts.

clue.text: A name is confused — result of this?

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone getting a name muddled up wonders if memory loss is the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description: a confused name is what memory loss produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, and forgetting or muddling people's names is a typical symptom.

clue.text: Love helping to give speech

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Someone who loves helping out agrees to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public address, a speech delivered on a ceremonial occasion.

clue.text: A curious sort of plant

blocks.note: taken as written
rum is British slang for odd or curious

explanation.surface: Someone describes a strange-looking specimen in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum, besides the drink, is an old British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a genus of plants with a hooded spathe, such as the lords-and-ladies of hedgerows.

clue.text: Improve on a repair

blocks.note: taken as written
a four-letter word for a repair or patch-up

explanation.surface: A handyman tries to do better than a botched fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Improve on' reads as one phrase, but 'on' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to change it so as to correct or better it.

clue.text: Thanks to an American prosecutor you get the facts

indicators.note: one thing added to another is attached after it, which fixes the order here

blocks.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A US lawyer is thanked for presenting the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thanks to' reads as 'because of', but it means the thanks are added to the prosecutor. Ta is everyday British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference or analysis.

clue.text: Preposition used in any amount of sentences

indicators.note: something used in a phrase is embedded within it, so the letters sit inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding that completes the picture

explanation.surface: A grammar teacher notes how often a certain preposition turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle 'amount of'. The surface is apt too: the old-fashioned preposition appears in many biblical sentences.
explanation.definitionFit: Unto is an archaic word meaning to or towards, a preposition familiar from the Bible.

clue.text: Tariff one’s found in hired transport

blocks.note: a tariff is a tax on imports
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fare card is displayed inside a cab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One’s' is 'one has', and 'found in' joins the wordplay to the definition, not placing a piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a car with driver hired for individual journeys, paid by a metered fare.

clue.text: No longer cares and pulls out

blocks.note: ex means former, no longer
to tend is to care for

explanation.surface: Someone stops caring and withdraws from a commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulls out' suggests withdrawal, but it means stretches out, lengthens.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something is to stretch or draw it out, as one pulls out a telescope.

clue.text: French friends set out in poor visibility

indicators.note: something laid out is opened and spread apart, which makes room for another piece inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
amis is French for friends

explanation.surface: Some French friends head off despite the fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' looks like departing, but SET opens out to hold the French friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea mist is fog rolling in from the sea, which reduces how far one can see.

clue.text: Once again sort out those of a certain age

indicators.note: sorting something out rearranges it, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone must once again organise a group of elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' belongs to the fodder; only 'out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Octogenarians are people aged between eighty and eighty-nine, a particular decade of life.
